features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures the applicant's real production experience with AI or LLM systems, especially attention to reliability, evaluation, guardrails, and operational hardening.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Academic degree level
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or academic qualification the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems with explicit control boundaries, supervision, permissions, or guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter gives credible, concrete evidence of practical data-structures-and-algorithms skill applied to real systems.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers through usable defaults, reduced friction, and service to internal users rather than policing them.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how much the letter substantiates its claims with concrete technical examples, named systems, mechanisms, scope, or measurements rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-relevant Go appears in the applicant's recent engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Does not provide meaningful evidence of Go use.
Mentions some Go exposure but not as a core language.
Presents Go as a major working language in production.
Presents Go as the principal or dominant language across core services.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter states the outcomes, consequences, or practical effects of the applicant's work rather than only naming activities.

levels.descriptor: Mostly lists duties or technologies with little sense of outcome.
Implies positive effect, but without a clear result.
States a clear before-and-after outcome for at least one contribution.
Shows vivid or quantified operational impact that explains what changed for the team.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages the applicant claims beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: Captures whether the letter is memorable, cohesive, and well-framed as a story rather than reading like a generic or disconnected checklist.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing hands-on adversarial or attacker-minded practice outside routine development work, especially through CTFs.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public or upstream codebases, from patches and dependency fixes to sustained maintenance, releases, and external-user accountability.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and self-directed depth of side projects or independent engineering work outside the day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational infrastructure or platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, systems, or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production engineering track record
features.description: Captures the depth, breadth, and direct ownership of professional production software delivery experience, including years in role, lifecycle responsibility, and shipped systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and convincingly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, automation, tooling, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Reliability and rigor mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, failure awareness, testing, correctness, and durable operation as core engineering values.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role-specific fit and motivation
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter explains why this exact role is compelling and maps the applicant's background to its stated mission and requirements.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures the depth and concreteness of hands-on experience assessing systems, designs, or code for security issues and validating remediation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation insight
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role as a systems-and-automation problem for scaling scarce security expertise, including its specific workflows and leverage.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal external security certifications or similar third-party validation.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
A baseline credential is mentioned, such as Security+, indicating foundational security study.
A stronger hands-on credential is mentioned, such as OSCP, indicating practical offensive testing ability.

features.name: Security philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful, role-relevant point of view about secure engineering work and why it matters.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinctive security philosophy beyond generic enthusiasm.
Shows broad positive sentiment about security or impact, but little deeper framing.
Expresses a clear philosophy about rigor, resilience, secure defaults, or invisible success.
Offers a memorable, specific philosophy that strongly reinforces fit for this kind of security work.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface correctness and professionalism of the prose, including spelling, grammar, proofreading, and copy-editing quality.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures miscellaneous low-recurrence constructs that do not cleanly belong to the main criteria, including coachability/collaboration and blended external security commitment signals.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear collaboration or internal-customer orientation.
Uses generic team language, but without a concrete sense of collaborators or users.
Explicitly mentions partnering with security engineers or serving developer teams.
Clearly frames success as collaborative enablement, including learning from specialists and building thoughtfully for other engineers.
